statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across 58 checks and seven representative paths.

page.framework: Next.js fragments within a server-rendered multi-page site
page.notes: Public German weather portal. Representative templates cover landing, listing, city forecast, interactive radar, editorial article, search results, and HTTP error recovery. Not covered: account/native-app-only, paid contentpass checkout, or destructive/commercial flows because they were not part of the public core weather journey.

checkOutcomes.method: Evidence selected from the catalog hint: compare heap snapshots for retained growth - a baseline, then one taken after repeating the interaction with `--interact` about 10x (the memory-tracer methodology: baseline -> repeat -> post -> compare). Performance.getMetrics (JSHeapUsedSize, Nodes) across the same before/after window is corroboration. If Chrome DevTools MCP is available, follow its memory-leak-debugging skill: capture baseline, target, and final snapshots, then use memlab or the provided comparison workflow rather than reading raw .heapsnapshot files directly. The package-native `heap` primitive remains the default path. This check is only meaningful where the page has a real intera
checkOutcomes.evidence: After one warm-up menu cycle, DOM nodes remained exactly 2,558 after 10 and 20 further cycles; heap fell after warm-up and changed only from 9.18MB to 9.59MB between cycles 10 and 20.

checkOutcomes.method: Evidence selected from the catalog hint: a single `heap` summary's totals (nodeCount, totalSelfSizeBytes, constructor population) plus Performance.getMetrics (Nodes, JSHeapUsedSize) give the current footprint to judge against the page's purpose. Chrome DevTools MCP heap snapshots and memlab snapshot analysis can provide the same memory distribution when available. Read summaries or derived analysis, never raw snapshots unless a dedicated heap-analysis tool is doing the analysis. The model chooses.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The baseline heap summary was 7.10MB self size and 108,750 snapshot nodes; the warmed same-session series settled near 9–10MB JS heap for this content-heavy page.

checkOutcomes.method: Evidence selected from the catalog hint: the `heap` summary by constructor (Detached* nodes) compared across a before/after pair shows a growing detached-DOM population; an `evaluate` probe can sample listener/timer counts (e.g. getEventListeners-style counting, or instrumenting addEventListener/setInterval) before and after the repeated interaction to spot growth. Chrome DevTools MCP heap snapshots plus the memory-leak-debugging skill's common-leak guidance can corroborate detached DOM, listeners, closures, globals, and unbounded caches. Caveat from the memory-tracer and Chrome DevTools MCP guidance: detached nodes can be intentional caches, so judge confidence rather than asserting a bug.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The same-session repeated menu test accumulated zero DOM nodes after warm-up, and the sampled live DOM reported no detached nodes.

paths.description: Homepage and national-weather landing template; inspected primary purpose, navigation, consent, preferences, performance, security, semantics, and network.
Germany forecast listing/index template, representing country and regional listings.
Berlin location-detail template, representing the core local forecast journey.
Interactive rain-radar template, representing map/loading and richer interaction surfaces.
Current news article template, representing editorial content and share/discovery surfaces.
Search results flow for Berlin, representing the primary place-finding form and result state.
Deliberate unknown URL, representing HTTP error messaging and recovery.

findings.summary: The consent wall interrupts content before any user request and is not exposed as a semantic modal.
findings.evidence: Load screenshots and the overlay probe show a fixed 780×493 custom DIV at z-index 900000 on desktop, with no role, aria-modal, label, <dialog>, or popover; city and article captures are entirely covered.
findings.suggestedFix: Present a compact, accessible consent dialog only when legally required; use <dialog> with showModal(), a clear accessible name, Escape/cancel behavior where allowed, focus containment, and equal access to privacy choices.

findings.summary: The consent UI is wider than a phone viewport and clips both primary choices.
findings.evidence: At 360px, layout reports scrollWidth 740px. The consent probe places “Akzeptieren und weiter” from x=-130 to 148.5 and the paid choice from x=229.5 to 507, so neither option is fully visible. Home and city layout reports show 380px horizontal overflow whenever this wall appears.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the fixed two-column desktop layout with a single-column mobile layout constrained by inline-size: min(100% - 2rem, ...); ensure every action remains fully visible without horizontal scrolling.

findings.summary: The site does not adapt to the user’s dark color preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-mode screenshot is visually identical to the light capture; computed color-scheme is “normal”, and stylesheet inspection found no prefers-color-scheme rule.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and provide dark surface/text tokens using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark(), including the consent experience.

findings.summary: Reduced-motion preference leaves smooth scrolling enabled.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the probe confirms the media query is active but html still computes scroll-behavior: smooth; stylesheet inspection found no reduced-motion branch.
findings.suggestedFix: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, switch scroll-behavior to auto and suppress nonessential animated media/transitions.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is slow on the primary landing page.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 6.9s (performance 0.74); the independent trace measured LCP 4.24s and FCP 2.87s. Both exceed the good LCP threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP element, prioritize its request, reduce render-blocking styles/scripts, and avoid making consent/layout work compete with primary content.

findings.summary: Render-blocking and unused/duplicated front-end code delay useful content.
findings.evidence: HAR identifies six parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets plus high-priority scripts; Lighthouse estimates 15KiB unused CSS, 33KiB unused JS, and 20KiB duplicated JS.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline only critical CSS, consolidate breakpoint styles, defer noncritical code, split by template, and remove duplicate/unused modules.

findings.summary: The viewport configuration disables user zoom.
findings.evidence: The DOM contains maximum-scale=1.0 and user-scalable=no; axe reports meta-viewport as critical and Lighthouse accessibility is 0.93.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and user-scalable restrictions so pinch zoom and text scaling remain available.

findings.summary: Several text elements fail minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: axe reports four serious color-contrast failures and 31 additional elements requiring review; Lighthouse independently fails the color-contrast audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background design tokens to meet WCAG AA in normal, high-contrast, and consent states; verify with axe and forced-colors/prefers-contrast.

findings.summary: Accessibility semantics and reading order contain repeatable defects.
findings.evidence: axe reports 37 invalid list items, duplicate/nested banner landmarks, heading-order failure, and uncovered content; Lighthouse also finds accessible-name/visible-label mismatches and positive tabindex.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore native list semantics, keep one top-level banner, put content in named landmarks, fix heading order, remove positive tabindex, and ensure accessible names contain visible labels.

findings.summary: Some controls are too small or lose a visible focus indicator.
findings.evidence: The control probe found 20×20 carousel buttons and a 27px-wide search submit control; focused search/menu links computed outline-style none in sampled states.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44×44 CSS-pixel hit areas where practical and use :focus-visible with a high-contrast outline that is never removed without replacement.

findings.summary: A JavaScript console error occurs during load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports “Refused to set unsafe header Accept-Encoding” and fails the errors-in-console audit.
findings.suggestedFix: Stop client code from setting forbidden request headers and confirm a clean Runtime/console log.

findings.summary: Image delivery and dimensions waste bandwidth and create avoidable layout risk.
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 40 images without dimensions, 65 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 30 oversized images, 43 without srcset, and 10 legacy-format images.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve intrinsic dimensions, lazy-load below-fold media, emit responsive srcset/sizes, and prefer AVIF/WebP while preserving appropriate SVG assets.

findings.summary: Defensive browser policy is incomplete and one cookie is insecurely scoped.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence finds no Content-Security-Policy or Permissions-Policy. Cookie evidence finds deflang without Secure and with SameSite=None despite first-party use.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, a least-privilege Permissions-Policy, and set the language cookie Secure with Lax or Strict SameSite unless cross-site use is demonstrated.

findings.summary: The public weather/search experience has no structured agent capability surface.
findings.evidence: The page is server-rendered and discoverable, but the platform probe found no WebMCP registration; Lighthouse’s agentic-browsing category scored 0.5.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose narrowly scoped, read-only agent tools for place search, current conditions, forecasts, and warnings, with explicit schemas and user control.

findings.summary: The landing page buries core weather content in a very long mixed feed.
findings.evidence: The mobile homepage is 9,045px tall and mixes forecasts, news, promotions, recommendations, webcams, maps, destination lists, and a large footer after the primary map.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize current conditions, forecast, radar, and warnings; collapse secondary discovery modules behind clear section links and defer offscreen rendering.

findings.summary: The consent choice architecture is visually coercive and hard to compare on mobile.
findings.evidence: The mobile probe shows “accept and continue” clipped on the left and the paid alternative clipped on the right, while privacy settings are secondary text links; users cannot view equal choices together.
findings.suggestedFix: Present equally legible accept, reject/customize, and paid options in one responsive view with neutral hierarchy and concise consequences.

findings.summary: The core local-forecast and article journeys can be blocked by an unusable consent step.
findings.evidence: Fresh mobile captures of both the Berlin detail and article templates show only the clipped consent wall rather than the requested forecast/article.
findings.suggestedFix: Make the consent step responsive and keyboard/screen-reader operable, preserve the requested destination, and return focus to the original task after the choice.

taskList.title: Rebuild the consent experience as an accessible, responsive, neutral dialog
Restore zoom, semantic structure, contrast, focus, and target sizing
Reduce LCP and remove render-blocking, unused, and duplicate code
Deploy CSP/Permissions-Policy and secure the language cookie
Add responsive image sizing, intrinsic dimensions, lazy loading, and modern formats
Add dark and reduced-motion preference styles
Refocus the homepage on forecast, radar, and warnings
Expose safe read-only weather and warning capabilities to agents
